voice: One brief can mean two very different projects. This is ScopeMatch.

label: 01 / Start with the real brief
voice: ScopeMatch helps freelancers and clients agree on what a website includes before work starts. Raka creates a surf school project and pastes Nadia's brief.

label: 02 / Turn vague words into concrete questions
voice: The brief suggests relevant questions from a curated library. Raka keeps booking and languages, then checks what is missing.

label: 03 / AI drafts. A person reviews.
voice: For details outside the library, Gemini can draft extra questions. The privacy notice appears before anything is sent. Raka reviews the options and their scope details, then adds a question. AI never answers or decides for either person.

label: 04 / Separate private links
voice: He locks the questions and gets separate private links.

label: 05 / The client's view
lead:
One shared brief.
Two private perspectives.
voice: Nadia opens her link on a phone. No account needed.

label: 06 / Answer independently, then seal
voice: Raka answers independently, then seals his choices. His answers stay hidden while Nadia is still deciding.

label: 07 / No peeking at the other person's answers
voice: Nadia imagines instant booking. She answers the same questions and seals her choices. Only then can either person compare.

label: 08 / Make the difference visible
voice: Their booking answers differ: a WhatsApp conversation versus an instant reservation. Visual examples make that difference concrete before work begins.

label: 09 / Propose a concrete decision
voice: Raka proposes WhatsApp booking. It remains a proposal until Nadia agrees or suggests an alternative.

label: 10 / Counter-propose with a reason
lead:
Discuss the difference.
Keep the reasoning.
voice: Nadia counter-proposes a request form with staff approval. She explains why: staff need to confirm lesson availability.

label: 11 / Confirm the same decision
voice: Raka confirms her proposal. The earlier proposal stays visible in the history.

label: 12 / Matching answers still need confirmation
voice: They also confirm the questions where their answers already match. A matching answer alone never counts as an agreed decision.

label: 13 / Review a usable scope document
voice: Once every decision is confirmed, ScopeMatch assembles the scope: included work, exclusions, client responsibilities, and acceptance criteria. Raka reviews it and sends version one.

label: 14 / A revision needs fresh confirmation
voice: He then adds a note and saves version two. The earlier confirmation resets, so an outdated version cannot become the agreement.

label: 15 / Both confirm the latest version

shots.lead:
Confirm the same version.
Then it is agreed.

voice: Raka and Nadia each confirm version two by name. Both confirmations now refer to the same version, and the document becomes agreed.

label: 16 / Download the actual agreed result
voice: The downloaded Markdown contains the original brief, decisions, scope, version, and confirmation records. This is the actual exported file.
ScopeMatch. Make the assumptions visible. Agree before work starts.
